name: Noiri
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Varkey, Vinod Wilson & Kishore Kumar Vunnamatla. 2018. A Sociolinguistic Study of Bareli/Pauri and Related Languages. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2018-011.
sources.note: Nothing; Table 7 lists Watters' 1987-88 Dhule survey (Paura, Vasava, Bhilori) and Sunil Mathew's 1995 Dungra Bhili survey (Dungra Bhil, Bhilala, Bhilori) as prior surveys; no Bhilori/Noiri phonology cited.

sources.citation: Watters, Stephen. 2013. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Bhils of Northern Dhule District. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2013-004. Dallas: SIL International. 133 pp. (fieldwork 1987-88; Glottolog 552859).
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (210-item IPA wordlist lexical similarity, recorded-text intelligibility, bilingualism, attitudes) of Vasave, Bhilori (Mundalwad), Noiri (Astamba), Pauri and Nahali; p.5 identifies the Satpuda Noiri/Bhilori and quotes Grierson's Nori of Bhopawar, doubting they are the same language. Appendix C wordlists (checked on rendered pp. 99-100) show segmental IPA only, no stress marks.

sources.citation: Varma, Siddheshwar. 1973. G. A. Grierson's Linguistic Survey of India: A Summary, Part II. Hoshiarpur: Vishveshvaranand Institute, Panjab University. 'Nori', para 586, pp. 1071-1072 (chapter 'Bhil dialects and Khandesi' = the Glottolog-listed Varma 1978 fascicle 'Bhil dialects and Khandesi: a linguistic analysis', viii+54 pp.).
sources.note: Nothing; a condensation of Grierson's two pages (sound correspondences, noun and verb inflexion). No accent/stress/tone content.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page noir1238 (Noiri; alt. Bhilori, Mathwadi; classification per Grierson 1907) and ISO 639-3 registry page for noi.
sources.note: Nothing; confirms that the only descriptive references Glottolog holds are Grierson 1907 (overview), Watters 2013 (overview) and Varma 1978 (minimal); ISO page lists no change-request documents.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.). 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX Pt III: Indo-Aryan Family, Central Group, The Bhil Languages, including Khandesi, Banjari or Labhani, Bahrupia, &c. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. Section 'Nori' pp. 105-106 + specimen No. 33 (Nori of Ali Rajpur, Bhopawar Agency).
sources.note: Nothing. The two-page Nori sketch gives only segmental notes (a pronounced as o, r dropped between vowels, loss of aspiration, soft > hard consonants as in doh 'ten', ho 'house', nasalisation as in Barel, cerebral l dropped in doa 'eye') plus noun/pronoun/verb inflexion. Whole-volume a full-text search for stress/accent/stress finds only the front-matter transcription convention ('When it is necessary to mark an accented syllable, the acute accent is used'); the Nori specimen carries no acute accents.

sources.citation: People's Linguistic Survey of India, Maharashtra volume (Marathi: Maharashtratil Bhasha; Arun Jakhade ed., 2013) and Madhya Pradesh volume (Devy et al., Orient BlackSwan, 2014-2017) -- chapters on Bhil-group varieties of the Satpudas (Bhilori/Noiri, Pawri, Nahali) and of Alirajpur/Barwani.

sources.citation: Mathew, Sunil. 1995. Dungra Bhili survey report. Ms. (SIL; covered Dungra Bhil, Bhilala and Bhilori of Baroda GJ and Jhabua/Alirajpur MP; cited in Varkey & Vunnamatla 2018 Table 7).

sources.note: Covers the northern (Alirajpur) Noiri/Bhilori area that Grierson's Nori belongs to; a survey wordlist report, unlikely but possible to carry phonetic notes on stress.

sources.citation: Any SIL / NLCI (New Life Computer Institute / Friends Missionary Prayer Band) 'Bhilori phonemic summary' or orthography write-up prepared for the Bhilori Bible-translation programme (Dhadgaon, Akrani tahsil). Existence inferred by analogy with 'Mathew, Sunil & Maya Susan. 2000. Dungra Bhil phonemic summary. Mumbai: FMPB' (cited in Payne 2006 for the sister variety duh); no record of a Bhilori one was seen.
